messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test failure and the current bug report suggest that ClassUtils.getShortClassName() malfunctions when given an array class, adding a semicolon to the end of the returned short class name (e.g., "String;" instead of "String").

From the code snippets:
- The entry method is getShortClassName(Class<?> cls). It simply extracts the class name string via cls.getName() and calls getShortClassName(String).
- In getShortClassName(String className), there is a piece of code commented as "Handle array encoding" and "Strip Object type encoding", but the actual logic for handling array class name syntax (which uses encoded representations like "[Ljava.lang.String;") is missing from the snippet. Instead, it just finds the last dot and extracts the substring after that as the short name, replacing inner class separators with dots.
- The class name of an array class in Java (e.g. String[].class) typically appears as "[Ljava.lang.String;".
- The existing code just extracts the substring after the last dot, so it extracts "String;" including the trailing semicolon, causing the bug.
- There is no special handling in getShortClassName(String) that correctly parses or strips the array prefix "[" or the trailing semicolon ";" which denote an array in JVM internal class notation.
- The bug report aligns with this diagnosis, describing semicolons introduced for arrays due to this omission.

Thus the root cause is missing parsing of array class name encoding in getShortClassName(String), causing the trailing semicolon present in the internal class name representation of arrays to be incorrectly included in the returned short class name. The code does not handle or decode the internal array encoding prefix "[" and the trailing ";" properly.

No evidence from recent bug reports is relevant here.

This explains why the test expecting "String[]" or "String" gets a failed assertion because it instead obtains a class name with a semicolon suffix.

The fix needs to add handling in getShortClassName(String) to correctly detect array encoded class names and transform them into clean readable short names, e.g. converting "[Ljava.lang.String;" into "String[]".

Summary:
- The array class names are encoded as "[L...;" in JVM notation.
- The existing code does not handle that encoding.
- It mistakenly returns the last token including the ";".
- So the trailing ";" appears in the short class name, causing test and user failures.

Recommended locations to fix:
- ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String)
- ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
